new_value: Fixed _peer_is_local_admin (messaging.py): RFC 3986 authority parsing strips [host]:port brackets properly and single :port suffix for other hosts; loopback classified via ipaddress for BOTH families so '127.0.0.1', '127.0.0.1:5683', '[::1]:5683', '[::1]:9999' are admin per contract. Spoof-safety retained: hostinfo is the transport-derived peer address, only genuine loopback literals grant admin. Cross-checked firmware coap_keys.c:49 lichen_coap_is_local_admin + Zephyr net_ipv6_is_addr_loopback (exact ::1/128): implemented explicit addr.ipv4_mapped deny-guard BEFORE .is_loopback because Python 3.11 ipaddress unwraps '::ffff:127.0.0.1' to True (verified empirically) — firmware semantics win, '::ffff:127.0.0.1' stays DENIED both sides, documented in docstring. Noted divergence: C server binds AF_INET6-only sockets so native IPv4 loopback exists only on the Python side; Zephyr link-local requires SLIP scope_id, Python has no transport identity so link-local stays untrusted (unchanged). Tests: TestLocalAdminAuthorityParsing 16-case matrix incl malformed/untrusted forms, plus e2e CREATED via '127.0.0.1' and '[::1]:9999'; tests/coap/test_messages_resource.py 144 passed.
